quote:
Try to keep the files as short as possible while keeping the context between the code parts by
- splitting your code into multiple files. Especially react components can and should be separated into atomic components and custom hooks.
statement: In frontend/**, code should be split into multiple short files; React components should be separated into atomic components and custom hooks.
In frontend/**, code should avoid repetition.

quote: - extracting types and interfaces into `.d.ts` files.
statement: In frontend/**, types and interfaces should be extracted into separate .d.ts files rather than declared inline in implementation files.

quote: We prefer lambda functions over the `function` keyword. Simple functions, that return a value can be shortened to one-liners.
statement: In frontend/**, functions should be written as arrow (lambda) functions assigned to const (e.g. `const addTwo = (x: number): number => x + 2`), not with the `function` keyword.

quote:
Names of functions should
- be as short as possible while clearly communicating their purpose.
- not include technical details, if not necessary.
statement: In frontend/**, function names should be as short as possible while clearly communicating their purpose and should not include unnecessary technical details (e.g. not `doStuffWithX`, `incrementXTwoTimesButNotRecursive`).
In frontend/**, function names should not use abbreviations (e.g. not `clcX`).

quote: To make the code as clear as possible to everyone, who will try to understand it, every function must have an [ESDoc](https://esdoc.org/).
statement: In frontend/**, every function must have an ESDoc/JSDoc comment (/** ... */) above it.

quote: Please make sure that your documenation can be read in a standard text editor (hard line breaks at ~120 characters, etc.).
statement: In frontend/**, function documentation comments should use hard line breaks at about 120 characters.

quote: - explain what the function does. If the explanation is longer than one line, then write a short introdoctory first line, followed by a break and then the longer explanation.
statement: In frontend/**, a function's ESDoc must explain what the function does; multi-line explanations must start with a short introductory first line, followed by a break and the longer explanation.

quote: - contain every parameter with the `@param name explaination` annotation, that explains the purpose of the parameter.
statement: In frontend/**, a function's ESDoc must contain a `@param name explanation` annotation for every parameter.

quote: - contain a `@return description` annotation if the return type isn't `void`, that explains the meaning of the value.
statement: In frontend/**, a function's ESDoc must contain a `@return description` annotation when the return type is not void (React components that always return the same DOM may omit it, per line 106).

quote: - contain `@throws ErrorClass description` annotations if the function throws runtime errors or doesn't catch errors from other method calls.
statement: In frontend/**, a function's ESDoc must contain `@throws ErrorClass description` annotations if the function throws or does not catch errors from called methods.

quote: - contain a blank line between the description and the annotation block.
statement: In frontend/**, a function's ESDoc must have a blank line between the description and the annotation block.

quote: The described annotations must appear in this order: `@param`, `@return`, `@throws`
statement: In frontend/**, ESDoc annotations must appear in the order @param, @return, @throws.

quote: Every exported type and interface must have an [ESDoc](https://esdoc.org/). No special annotations are needed.
statement: In frontend/**, every exported type alias and interface must have an ESDoc comment.

quote:
React components
- must be functional. Use the `React.FC` type.
statement: In frontend/**, React components must be function components, not class components.

quote: - must be functional. Use the `React.FC` type.
statement: In frontend/**, React components must be typed with `React.FC` (e.g. `export const X: React.FC<XProps> = (...) => ...`).

quote: - should use the [`useCallback`](https://reactjs.org/docs/hooks-reference.html#usecallback) hook where possible.
statement: In frontend/**, React components should wrap their callbacks/event handlers in the `useCallback` hook where possible.
In frontend/**, React components should not use inline function expressions (e.g. inline arrow functions in JSX props); use memoized callbacks instead.

quote: - should use [custom hooks](https://reactjs.org/docs/hooks-custom.html) to extract long functions to reduce the number of lines in the component file.
statement: In frontend/**, React components should extract long functions into custom hooks to keep component files short.

quote: - must be placed in files that have the same name as the component, but in [kebab-case](https://stackoverflow.com/a/17820138). This file can also contain the interface for the properties.
statement: In frontend/**, each React component must live in a file named after the component in kebab-case (e.g. IncrementNumberButton in increment-number-button.tsx); the file may also contain the component's props interface.
In frontend/**, React components should be named in PascalCase.

quote: - Don't log directly to the console.
statement: In frontend/**, code must not log directly to the console (console.log/warn/error etc.).
In frontend/**, logging must go through the `Logger` class from frontend/src/utils/logger.ts.

quote: - Create one instance of `Logger` per file.
statement: In frontend/**, each file that logs must create its own single module-level `Logger` instance (e.g. `const logger = new Logger('IncrementNumberButton')`).

quote: Don't pass or share the instances.
statement: In frontend/**, `Logger` instances must not be passed as arguments, exported or shared between files.

quote: - The first argument of the constructor is the scope. Use the name of the class or component whose behaviour you want to log or choose an explanatory name.
statement: In frontend/**, the first argument (scope) of `new Logger(...)` should be the name of the class or component being logged, or another explanatory name.

quote: - If you want to add a sub scope (because e.g. you have two components that are similar or are used together, like the sub-classes of the iframe communicator), separate the main and sub scope with " > ".
statement: In frontend/**, a Logger scope with a sub scope must separate main and sub scope with " > " (e.g. `new Logger('Main > Sub')`).

quote: - Scopes should be upper camel case.
statement: In frontend/**, Logger scope strings should be UpperCamelCase.

quote: - Log messages should never start with a lowercase letter.
statement: In frontend/**, log messages passed to Logger methods should not start with a lowercase letter.

quote: - Log messages should never end with a colon or white space.
statement: In frontend/**, log messages passed to Logger methods should not end with a colon or whitespace.
In the repository root lint scope, code should not contain `debugger` statements.
In the repository root lint scope, code should not have unused variables; unused arguments are allowed only if named with underscores only (^_+$).
In the repository root lint scope, TypeScript code should not have unused variables; unused arguments are allowed only if named ^_+$.
In the repository root lint scope, imports used only as types must use `import type` (type annotations in import() are allowed).
In the repository root lint scope, tests should not be disabled (no xit/xdescribe/test.skip).
In the repository root lint scope, tests must not be focused (no fit/fdescribe/test.only).
In the repository root lint scope, tests and describe blocks in the same scope must not share identical titles.
In the repository root lint scope, `expect()` must be used validly (one argument, followed by a matcher call, async matchers awaited).
In backend/**, code should not contain `debugger` statements (maxWarnings 0 makes any warning fail lint).

quote: backend/.oxlintrc.json:11 "hedgedoc-local/correct-logger-context": "error" -- "Ensure logger context strings match the method name where they are called"
statement: In backend/**, a call `this.logger.<error|log|warn|debug|verbose>(message, context)` with a string-literal second argument must pass as context the name of the enclosing class method (MethodDefinition), e.g. `this.logger.log('Hello', 'exampleMethod')` inside `exampleMethod()`.
scope: backend/src/**, backend/test/** class methods using this.logger

statement: In backend/**, TypeScript code should not have unused variables; unused arguments are allowed only if named with underscores only (^_+$).
In backend/**, returned promises must always be awaited (`return await promise`), not returned bare.
In backend/**, code must not stringify objects whose toString() is the default Object.prototype.toString (no "[object Object]" in template literals or String() calls).
In backend test files (backend/test/**, backend/src/**/*.spec.ts), referencing unbound methods is not checked (typescript/unbound-method turned off).
In backend test files, assigning `any`-typed values is not checked (typescript/no-unsafe-assignment turned off).
In backend test files, passing `any`-typed arguments is not checked (typescript/no-unsafe-argument turned off).
In backend test files, member access on `any`-typed values is not checked (typescript/no-unsafe-member-access turned off).
In backend test files, async functions without an await are allowed (typescript/require-await turned off).
In backend test files, functions are not required to declare explicit return types (typescript/explicit-function-return-type turned off).
In backend test files, useless default assignments are not checked (typescript/no-useless-default-assignment turned off).
In backend test files, `expect()` calls outside of it/test blocks are allowed (jest/no-standalone-expect turned off).
In commons/**, tests should not be disabled (no xit/xdescribe/test.skip); maxWarnings 0 makes warnings fail lint.
In commons/**, tests must not be focused (no fit/fdescribe/test.only).
In commons/**, tests and describe blocks in the same scope must not share identical titles.
In commons/**, `expect()` must be used validly (one argument, followed by a matcher call, async matchers awaited).
In frontend/**, code should not contain `debugger` statements (maxWarnings 0 makes any warning fail lint).
In frontend/**, imports used only as types must use `import type` (type annotations via import() are allowed).
In frontend/**, tests should not be disabled (no xit/xdescribe/test.skip).
In frontend/**, tests must not be focused (no fit/fdescribe/test.only).
In frontend/**, tests and describe blocks in the same scope must not share identical titles.
In frontend/**, `expect()` must be used validly (one argument, followed by a matcher call, async matchers awaited).
In frontend/**, every test must contain at least one assertion, i.e. a call matching expect*, screen.* or test*.

quote: frontend/.oxlintrc.json:25 "hedgedoc-frontend/translation-keys": "warn" -- "Checks that used translation keys exist in en.json"
statement: In frontend/**, static translation keys passed as the first argument to `t(...)` or `useTranslatedText(...)`, or as the `i18nKey` prop of `<Trans>`, must exist in frontend/locales/en.json (rule level warn, but maxWarnings 0 fails lint).
scope: frontend/src/** components and hooks using translations

statement: In frontend/**, plain `` elements are allowed instead of next/image (nextjs/no-img-element turned off).
In html-to-react/**, tests should not be disabled (no xit/xdescribe/test.skip).
In html-to-react/**, tests must not be focused (no fit/fdescribe/test.only).
In html-to-react/**, tests and describe blocks in the same scope must not share identical titles.
In html-to-react/**, `expect()` must be used validly (one argument, followed by a matcher call, async matchers awaited).
In markdown-it-plugins/**, tests should not be disabled (no xit/xdescribe/test.skip).
In markdown-it-plugins/**, tests must not be focused (no fit/fdescribe/test.only).
In markdown-it-plugins/**, tests and describe blocks in the same scope must not share identical titles.
In markdown-it-plugins/**, `expect()` must be used validly (one argument, followed by a matcher call, async matchers awaited).

quote:
Each of those files (except `auth.config.ts` which is discussed later) consists of three parts:

1. An interface
2. A Joi schema
3. A default export
statement: In backend/src/config/*.config.ts (except auth.config.ts), each config file should consist of a config interface, a validation schema, and a default export that builds and validates the config object.

quote: All enums that are used in here are put in their own files with the extension `.enum.ts`.
statement: In backend/src/config/**, enums used in config interfaces must be defined in their own files with the `.enum.ts` extension.

quote: The most important part here is that each value ends with `.label()`. This names the environment variable that corresponds to each config option.
statement: In backend/src/config/*.config.ts, every schema value must end with `.label()` naming the corresponding environment variable (e.g. HD_...).

quote: 2. The error messages are piped into the util method `replaceAuthErrorsWithEnvironmentVariables`.
statement: In backend/src/config/auth.config.ts, validation error messages should be passed through the util `replaceAuthErrorsWithEnvironmentVariables` to map them to user-defined environment variable names.

quote: Some config files also have a `.mock.ts` file which defines the configuration for the e2e tests. Those files just contain the default export and return the mock config object.
statement: In backend/src/config/**, e2e mock config files must be named `*.mock.ts` and contain only a default export returning the mock config object.

quote: In HedgeDoc 2, we use an event system based on [EventEmitter2][eventemitter2]. It's used to reduce circular dependencies between different services and inform these services about changes.
statement: In backend/src/**, services should be informed about changes via the NestJS EventEmitter2-based event system rather than direct service dependencies, to avoid circular dependencies.

quote: The config for the `EventEmitterModule` is stored in `events.ts` and exported as `eventModuleConfig`. In the same file enums for the event keys are defined.
statement: In backend/src/events.ts, the EventEmitterModule config must be exported as `eventModuleConfig` and the event-key enums must be defined in that same file.

quote: In the enum definition a comment should tell you what exactly this value should be.
statement: In backend/src/events.ts, each event-key enum member should carry a comment describing the value sent with that event.

quote:
Each storage backend needs to implement an interface with three methods:

- `saveFile(uuid, buffer, fileType)` ... - `deleteFile(uuid, metadata)` ... - `getFileUrl(uuid, metadata)`
statement: In backend/src/media/backends/**, each media storage backend must implement the media backend interface (backend/src/media/media-backend.interface.ts) with saveFile(uuid, buffer, fileType), deleteFile(uuid, metadata) and getFileUrl(uuid, metadata).

quote: Because we need to have empty constructors in our entity classes for TypeORM to work, the actual constructor is a separate `create` method.
statement: In backend entity classes, constructors must be empty and instances must be built via a separate static `create` method.

quote: - Only require the non-optional properties of the corresponding entity
statement: In backend entity classes, the static `create` method should only take the entity's non-optional properties as parameters (exceptions must be mentioned in the method documentation).
In backend entity classes, the static `create` method should have no optional parameters (unless documented as an exception).

quote: - Have no lists which can be empty (so probably most of them)
statement: In backend entity classes, the static `create` method should not take list parameters that can be empty (unless documented as an exception).

quote: - Should either return a complete and fully useable instance or return a Pick/Omit type.
statement: In backend entity classes, the static `create` method should return either a complete, fully usable instance or a Pick/Omit type of the entity.

quote: Therefore, the migrations and database types use their own CommonJS package.
statement: Knex migrations and database types must live in their own CommonJS package (not import TypeScript/ESM code from the backend or commons packages).

quote: All HTML should be properly sanitized using a dedicated sanitisation library (such as [dompurify](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dompurify) for node/js) before being passed to this library
statement: Code using html-to-react should sanitize HTML with a dedicated sanitizer such as dompurify before passing it to the library.

quote: The `preprocessNodes` function should return a valid `htmlparser2` node tree.
statement: A `preprocessNodes` function passed to html-to-react should return a valid htmlparser2 node tree.
